item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-67a39df98c2ca828","start_unit":14,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"In 2023, Bangladesh hosted more than 730,000 Rohingya refugees who faced restrictions on education, livelihoods, movement, and community-led schools; authorities had relocated about 30,000 to Bhasan Char, where HRW reported movement restrictions and shortages, while camp authorities failed to provide adequate protection or prosecute armed-group and criminal violence.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly describes conditions and policies in or continuing into 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Attributes restrictions and protection failures to Bangladesh authorities and camp authorities under the government.","limitations":["HRW reports conditions and allegations; this source does not establish Sheikh Hasina’s personal direction for each action."]},{"source_id":"SRC-67a39df98c2ca828","start_unit":16,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"The 2023 Rohingya Joint Response Plan received less than one-third of the requested US$876 million, leading WFP to cut food rations by one-third; Bangladesh nevertheless pursued a pilot Rohingya repatriation process with Myanmar that HRW characterized as involving coercion and deception, despite the absence of conditions for safe, sustainable, and dignified return.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","3B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly describes the 2023 humanitarian funding and repatriation context.","ruler_attribution":"Attributes the repatriation initiative to the Bangladesh government; ration cuts are attributed primarily to donor shortfall and WFP action.","limitations":["The source does not quantify Bangladesh’s own funding contribution or establish that Hasina personally ordered coercive practices."]},{"source_id":"SRC-60f05b7497b84bd8","start_unit":28,"end_unit":29,"fact_summary":"UNHCR describes Bangladesh as hosting more than one million stateless Rohingya refugees in highly congested camps in Cox’s Bazar and Bhasan Char, dependent on humanitarian assistance for protection, food, water, shelter, and health; UNHCR supports the government in providing services and protection, including for women, children, and people with disabilities.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8","6B.10","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The page is current, but describes an ongoing displacement situation that includes the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"Attributes hosting and service provision to the Government of Bangladesh, with UNHCR support.","limitations":["The supplied page does not provide a 2023-specific outcome assessment or distinguish central-government action from humanitarian-agency action."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8f138d3bfe16aac4","start_unit":11,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"RSF identifies Sheikh Hasina as Bangladesh’s prime minister since 2009 and describes the Digital Security Act as containing vague offenses that enabled prosecution and self-censorship of journalists and bloggers; it reports that the law was used against about 400 people, including more than 70 journalists and bloggers, and that ruling-party supporters harassed or attacked reporters.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.3","3B.8","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The page was published in 2021 and describes the legal and political system inherited into 2023; it does not document a 2023-specific incident.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributes the legal framework and political pattern to Hasina’s government and describes party supporters as enforcers.","limitations":["Evidence is primarily historical and not a contemporaneous 2023 assessment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fff6bf8295e15d2d","start_unit":10,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"Bangladesh’s National Board of Revenue portal provided budget access by financial year, including 2022–2023 and 2023–2024, and listed budget, finance-law, tax-law, customs, VAT, and revenue materials; the page also reported revenue publications through June 2023.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.6","5B.7","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly covers fiscal-year materials and revenue reporting relevant to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Shows state administrative publication and budget infrastructure under the government; it does not identify Hasina’s personal role.","limitations":["The page lists materials and systems but does not establish execution quality, macroeconomic effects, or independent audit."]},{"source_id":"SRC-11520a27d08a6ee5","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In March 2023, the UN Special Envoy thanked Bangladesh for its humanity and generosity in hosting more than one million Rohingya refugees for over five years, while also recording Bangladesh’s position that the situation was unsustainable; the UN emphasized that any return must be safe, voluntary, dignified, and address citizenship, movement, land, education, and livelihoods.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","3B.7","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly dated 16 March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Credits the Government of Bangladesh with hosting refugees and conveys its stated position on sustainability and return.","limitations":["The statement evaluates Bangladesh’s hosting role but does not assess all domestic policies toward refugees or Hasina’s personal decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-85f502fb978bbfb8","start_unit":4,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reports broad development gains associated with Bangladesh’s long-term development trajectory: gender parity in school enrollment, life expectancy above 70, near-universal electricity, major reductions in maternal and under-five mortality, 2023 net primary enrollment of 93.1%, and extensive climate-resilience, social-protection, infrastructure, and Rohingya-support programs; it also notes persistent institutional weaknesses and the need for better service delivery and inclusive job creation.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Includes a 2023 enrollment indicator and longer-run outcomes relevant to the period; the page was updated later and some figures are retrospective.","ruler_attribution":"Attributes outcomes to Bangladesh’s development strategy and government partnership with the World Bank, while recognizing external financing and implementation support.","limitations":["The source does not isolate Hasina’s marginal contribution from prior governments, donors, subnational actors, or World Bank programs; some displayed figures postdate 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4c049e7138bbaf9c","start_unit":2,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"A November 2023 World Bank results brief reports Bangladesh’s development gains, including reduced extreme poverty to 5.0% in 2022, gender parity in secondary enrollment, universal electricity access, increased female labor participation, climate-resilience investments, and shelter and support for more than one million Rohingya refugees; it also identifies 2023-era pressures including inflation, energy shortages, balance-of-payments deficits, revenue shortfalls, and climate vulnerability.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly published in November 2023 and reports outcomes through 2022 with ongoing programs and 2023 conditions.","ruler_attribution":"Attributes achievements to the long-running Government of Bangladesh–World Bank partnership and government development frameworks, not solely to Hasina.","limitations":["The brief is partnership-level evidence and cannot establish personal causation, distributional equality across all groups, or full 2023 execution."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c756737799580cc6","start_unit":23,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"A 2023 Bangladesh social-protection assessment found an evolving system under the NSSS, with financing expanded and coverage reaching about half the population by 2022; its overall score was 3.4/4, with strengths in fiscal sustainability, coherence, and responsiveness but weaker inclusiveness and incentive compatibility, including persistent targeting, adequacy, and vulnerable-group inclusion problems.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.7","6B.8","6B.9","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The assessment is explicitly identified as the 2023 assessment.","ruler_attribution":"Attributes the system to the Cabinet Division, Planning Commission, NSSS, and government reforms; it does not assign personal responsibility to Hasina.","limitations":["The supplied page summarizes the assessment rather than providing its underlying indicators or identifying 2023 year-end outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-dcc1960c1714b8d4","start_unit":6,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"A 2024 retrospective article alleges that Hasina’s government politicized police recruitment, postings, and promotions; used police and courts against opposition protests; retained restrictive speech provisions in the 2023 Cyber Security Act; and rewarded officials associated with partisan enforcement despite allegations of extrajudicial killings and enforced disappearances.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.5","4B.6","4B.9","7B.5","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published in August 2024 but describes conduct and institutional conditions extending through 2023 and the 2024 election period.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributes politicization, appointments, enforcement, and legal choices to Hasina’s government.","limitations":["This is a retrospective newspaper analysis containing allegations and characterizations; several examples concern 2014, 2018, or 2024 rather than 2023 alone."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c77aeb9304b128d6","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"In April 2023, the International Court of Justice extended Myanmar’s deadline for filing its counter-memorial in the Rohingya genocide case to 24 May 2023; the order records that Myanmar was required to submit periodic reports on provisional measures and that access to witnesses in Bangladesh was considered unlikely.","question_ids":["2B.7","2B.9","6B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Directly dated 6 April 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The order concerns Myanmar and the ICJ; it provides contextual evidence about the Rohingya crisis but no direct attribution to Hasina or Bangladesh policy.","limitations":["No material fact about Sheikh Hasina’s conduct is established beyond the cross-border legal and humanitarian context."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d3dd24196c37303a","start_unit":2,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In her September 2023 UNGA speech, Hasina stated that Bangladesh had reduced poverty and extreme poverty, increased social-safety-net support, introduced a universal pension scheme, expanded stipends and women’s empowerment measures, funded climate adaptation, provided affordable food to ten million low-income people, pursued the Delta Plan 2100, supported Rohingya shelter, and reaffirmed commitments to disarmament, human rights, democracy, rule of law, and freedom of expression.","question_ids":["1B.4","1B.10","2B.1","2B.7","3B.7","4B.1","4B.3","5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","7B.1","7B.8","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly dated September 2023 and records the ruler’s stated program and claimed implementation.","ruler_attribution":"Direct first-person account of Hasina’s stated policies, commitments, and claimed outcomes.","limitations":["Claims are self-reported in a political speech and are not independently verified by this document; speech statements alone do not establish implementation or outcome causation."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus contains several pages published after 2023 or retrospective summaries; those facts are marked with period-fit limitations and should not be treated as contemporaneous proof unless explicitly dated.","No supplied document provides material evidence about nuclear weapons, proliferation controls, AI or biological-risk safeguards, or Sheikh Hasina’s personal financial conflicts and asset accountability during 2023."]}
